headline: Joint and topological model inference for longitudinal and spatio-temporal biomedical data
label: Longitudinal Model Inference Frameworks
summary: Recent bioinformatics work pairs longitudinal biomarker data with joint survival and topological model-selection methods.
synthesis: The dominant thread is statistical and machine-learning inference that links longitudinal or spatio-temporal measurements to an outcome or mechanistic model. A preprint builds AI-based aging resilience metrics from longitudinal clinical records of baboons and rhesus macaques, using recurrent neural network and random forest models. A published bioinformatics method, JM-NCC, jointly models longitudinal biomarkers and competing-risk survival within nested case-control designs, applied to TEDDY microbiome data. A second published pipeline combines approximate Bayesian computation with topological data analysis for parameter inference and model selection in spatio-temporal models, validated on tumour-induced angiogenesis. The distinguishing element is the use of topology-based criteria for model selection, alongside joint longitudinal-survival estimation in nested designs.
